Compare co-expression neighborhoods across species

Source: R/comparison.R
compare_neighborhoods.Rd

For each ortholog pair, tests whether co-expression neighborhoods are conserved between species using hypergeometric tests in both directions.

Usage

compare_neighborhoods(net1, net2, orthologs, n_cores = 1L)

Arguments

net1

Network object for species 1 (output of compute_network()).

net2

Network object for species 2 (output of compute_network()).

orthologs

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, and hog (output of prepare_orthologs()).

n_cores

Number of threads for parallel computation (default 1).

Value

A data frame with columns:

gene1

Gene identifier for species 1

gene2

Gene identifier for species 2

hog

Ortholog group identifier

species1.neigh

Number of neighbors of gene1 gene in net1

species1.ortho.neigh

Number of ortholog-mapped neighbors from net2, excluding the gene1 gene itself

species1.neigh.overlap

Intersection size

species1.p_value_con

Upper-tail hypergeometric p-value for conservation (direction 1); 1 when the overlap is 0 or 1

species1.p_value_div

Lower-tail hypergeometric p-value for divergence (direction 1)

species1.p_value_gt

\(P(X > x)\), ungated (direction 1)

species1.p_value_eq

\(P(X = x)\) (direction 1)

species1.effect_size

Fold enrichment (direction 1). Values > 1 indicate conservation, < 1 indicate divergence.

species2.neigh

Number of neighbors of gene2 gene in net2

species2.ortho.neigh

Number of ortholog-mapped neighbors from net1, excluding the gene2 gene itself

species2.neigh.overlap

Intersection size

species2.p_value_con

Upper-tail hypergeometric p-value for conservation (direction 2); 1 when the overlap is 0 or 1

species2.p_value_div

Lower-tail hypergeometric p-value for divergence (direction 2)

species2.p_value_gt

\(P(X > x)\), ungated (direction 2)

species2.p_value_eq

\(P(X = x)\) (direction 2)

species2.effect_size

Fold enrichment (direction 2). Values > 1 indicate conservation, < 1 indicate divergence.

species1.jaccard

Jaccard index of neighborhood overlap (direction 1): intersection / union of anchor and ortholog-mapped neighbors. Range \([0, 1]\).

species2.jaccard

Jaccard index of neighborhood overlap (direction 2).

species1.urn

Hypergeometric population for direction 1: the number of genes in net1 less the anchor gene itself. Constant within a call. Downstream power uses it directly rather than reconstructing it from the effect sizes.

species2.urn

Hypergeometric population for direction 2 (genes in net2 less the anchor). Differs from species1.urn whenever the two networks differ in size.

Details

For an ortholog pair (A in species 1, B in species 2) and direction 1 (anchor A), the neighbourhood of A in net1 (size \(m\)) is tested against the set of species-1 orthologs of B's neighbours in net2 (size \(k\)); \(x\) is their intersection. The urn excludes the anchor gene: A is never its own neighbour, it is dropped from the mapped set, and the hypergeometric population is the other \(N - 1\) network genes. species1.p_value_con is \(P(X \ge x)\) and keeps the gate of the original RComPlEx R Markdown (not the paper): it is reported as 1 when \(x \le 1\). species1.p_value_gt (\(P(X > x)\)) and species1.p_value_eq (\(P(X = x)\)) are ungated so that p_value_gt + U * p_value_eq is a randomized p-value, exactly uniform under the null (used by summarize_comparison() to estimate pi0). The effect size \((x / k) / (m / (N - 1))\) is computed for every \(x\) (1 when \(m = 0\) or \(k = 0\)). Direction 2 is symmetric.

Ortholog preparation for de novo transcriptomes

When working with de novo transcriptome assemblies, it is critical to filter ortholog tables to expressed genes before applying any maximum-paralogs filter. De novo assemblies can produce 10–50x more gene models than are actually expressed (e.g. 205K models but only 14K expressed). Unexpressed fragments inflate paralog counts per ortholog group, causing the paralogs filter to discard groups that would pass if only expressed members were counted. Failing to do this can reduce the usable gene set by 40–70% and eliminate all statistical power from the hypergeometric test.

Recommended workflow:

  1. Build expression matrices for both species

  2. Filter ortholog table to genes present in expression data

  3. Apply maximum-paralogs filter on the reduced ortholog table

  4. Compute networks and run comparison

Gene universe

Networks are built on all supplied genes and \(N\) is the number of genes in the anchor network, as in Netotea et al. (2014). The canonical ComPlEx implementations (RComPlEx.Rmd, ComPlEx_python) instead restrict the expression tables to genes with an ortholog before building the networks, which changes neighbourhoods, thresholds and therefore the calls. rcomplex reproduces those implementations only when the expression matrices are restricted the same way before compute_network() (tests/testthat/test-equivalence.R).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
comparison <- compare_neighborhoods(net_A, net_B, orthologs)
head(comparison[, c(
  "gene1", "gene2", "hog",
  "species1.effect_size"
)])
} # }
